name: PBB Account
shortDescription: Local canonical identity and OAuth-style sign-in for participating PBB applications on a deployed node.
longDescription: PBB Account provides a local identity authority and shared sign-in surface for participating applications. It keeps identity available inside the node boundary when an upstream route is unavailable.
Its current contracts are OAuth-like integration contracts for the PBB stack, not a claim of complete OpenID Connect conformance or compatibility with every third-party relying party.

readiness.note: Canonical local identity and application sign-in integrations are implemented across participating services.
remainingWork: Complete production credential and key rotation procedures.
Harden role and claim contracts for every deployed relying application.
Do not advertise full OpenID Connect conformance without a separate verification effort.

nodeRole: Acts as the local identity authority so participating applications can recognize one governed user identity without depending on a public cloud login route.
localBehavior: Sign-in and local identity lookup continue while Account and its database are healthy.
Identity records remain within the configured node data boundary.
connectivityBehavior: Cross-node identity exchange is not implied by local sign-in.
External identity federation requires an explicit, separately reviewed integration.
operationalConsiderations: Back up identity data and signing material under a documented recovery procedure.
Coordinate client identifiers, redirect routes, and role mappings for each application.
securityBoundary: Keep administrative access and secrets inside the managed node boundary.
OAuth-style support must not be presented as certified full OIDC support.

faqs.question: Is PBB Account a complete OpenID Connect provider?
faqs.answer: No. PBB Account provides a shared local identity and sign-in service for participating PBB apps, but it is not presented as a complete OpenID Connect service.

faqs.question: Can users sign in without internet access?
faqs.answer: Yes, as long as PBB Account, its stored data, and the app are working on the local PBB network.

faqs.question: Does one account automatically work on every PBB node?
faqs.answer: No. Accounts work across nodes only when the deployment owner deliberately connects them and sets rules for how identities are managed.

faqs.question: Who defines application roles and permissions?
faqs.answer: The deployment owner decides which roles people receive. Each app must then check those roles before allowing access to protected features.

faqs.question: What must operators protect during recovery?
faqs.answer: Operators must protect account records, security keys, app connection settings, and the documented steps used to restore access safely.
